selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: In the comparison, what was the first servant told to do with the small amount of money?
questions.answer: He was told to buy clothes from a certain kind of cloth.

questions.question: What extra thing was put in the second servant’s pocket besides the money?
questions.answer: A written note about a task he needed to do.

questions.question: Why would a wise person know that the larger amount of money was not mainly for buying clothes?
questions.answer: Because a very nice outfit had already been bought with much less money, so the bigger amount had to be for a more important purpose.

questions.question: What mistake did the second servant make before spending the money?
questions.answer: He did not read the note that explained what he was supposed to do.

questions.question: What did the second servant do after looking at the first servant?
questions.answer: He copied him and spent all the money on clothing.

questions.question: How was the clothing bought by the second servant described compared with the first servant’s?
questions.answer: It was much poorer and far worse.

questions.question: How did the employer respond to the second servant’s action?
questions.answer: He strongly scolded him and punished him.

questions.question: What lesson does the comparison teach about human abilities and life?
questions.answer: Our abilities were not given just for bodily pleasure and worldly living; they were given for a higher purpose.

questions.question: According to the passage, what happens if a person uses life only like an animal?
questions.answer: That person falls lower than animals even though he was given much more.

questions.question: What warning is given to the nafs and the friend at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: They are warned not to waste life’s gifts on short-lived desires.

questions.question: How much money did the first servant receive, and what was it for?
questions.answer: He received twenty gold pieces to have clothing made.

questions.question: How much money did the second servant receive?
questions.answer: He received one thousand gold pieces.

questions.question: What does the huge difference in the two amounts suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that the second servant had a much bigger and more important duty.

questions.question: What should the second servant have done first after receiving the note and the money?
questions.answer: He should have read the note and followed its instructions.

questions.question: Why was it foolish for the second servant to spend everything on clothes?
questions.answer: Because he ignored the real job he had been sent to do.

questions.question: What caused the second servant to choose the wrong action?
questions.answer: He followed what another servant did instead of understanding his own assignment.

questions.question: In the lesson after the comparison, what does “capital” of life mean?
questions.answer: It means the valuable abilities and opportunities given to a person.

questions.question: What are people told not to spend this life capital on?
questions.answer: They are told not to waste it on bodily cravings and temporary worldly fun.

questions.question: According to the passage, how can a human become worse than an animal?
questions.answer: By using great human gifts only for low desires.

questions.question: What is the moral of the comparison in simple words?
questions.answer: Don’t waste the precious gifts of life on small and passing things.

questions.question: What is the main point of the comparison at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: Human powers were not created only to gain worldly comfort like animals.

questions.question: What did the first servant manage to buy with only a little money?
questions.answer: A very nice set of clothes.

questions.question: What shows that the second servant had a special mission besides spending money?
questions.answer: He was sent with a written message and a large amount of money to handle some business.

questions.question: What important clue did the second servant ignore?
questions.answer: He ignored the written instructions in his pocket.

title: Warning to the Wicked and the Self Explanation of Misuse Through a Parable and Awakening the Self
